title: Notes can only be opened with a mouse: rows are not focusable and have no key handler
evidence: Rows are plain li elements with a delegated click listener (app.js:30-33). Driven: the li tabIndex is -1, so Tab never reaches them. Opening a note is the main task. WCAG 2.1.1 (Level A).
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user tabs from Search to New note and then to the editor. They cannot select an existing note at all.
remediation: Render each title as a button (or a link, or an li with role=option in a listbox) that has a name and Enter/Space activation. Give the selected one aria-current.

title: Note title is written into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS)
evidence: app.js:10-11 builds the list row from n.title with a template string assigned through innerHTML. The title comes from the #title input and is persisted to localStorage (store.js:16). Driven in Chromium: the title produced two alert dialogs after reload.
failing_case: Create a note, set the title to , wait 500 ms, reload. The script runs on every page load and on every list render, and it runs again for any note imported or synced into localStorage from another source.
remediation: Build each row with createElement and textContent, or pass every interpolated value through one escape function. Do the same for every other innerHTML sink.

title: Unguarded JSON.parse at load: one corrupt value blanks the whole app
evidence: Driven: localStorage 'notes' set to '{bad', reload. store.js throws, so `notes` is never declared. app.js then fails with 'notes is not defined', the list has 0 children, and the New button is dead. There is no recovery path and no version field on the saved shape.
failing_case: A partial write, a manual edit, or a shape from another version leaves invalid JSON in 'notes'. Every later load shows an empty broken page, and the next successful save would overwrite the stored data if the app ever recovered.
remediation: Wrap load in try/catch, keep a copy of the raw string under a backup key, validate each record's fields, and store a schema version.

title: Debounced save writes to whatever note is current when the timer fires
evidence: scheduleSave (store.js:13-21) reads both the target note (currentNote) and the field values when the 500 ms timer fires, not when the edit happened. Driven: edited note A's body, clicked note B within 500 ms, waited. localStorage still held A with body 'a', and only B's updated stamp changed.
failing_case: Type in note A, click note B within half a second. openNote replaces the input values and currentNote before the timer fires, so A's edit is discarded and B's timestamp is bumped with B's own text.
remediation: Capture the target note and the field values when the edit happens, or flush the pending save inside openNote before switching. Keep one writer per note.

title: Fixed 1200 px container and 300 px sidebar: the page scrolls sideways on phones and at 200% zoom
evidence: Driven at 390 px wide: document scrollWidth 1222. styles.css:7 adds a 300 px fixed first column. WCAG 1.4.10 reflow (AA).
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the user must scroll horizontally to reach the editor. At 200% zoom on a 1360 px screen the same happens.
remediation: Use max-width: 1200px with width: 100%, and a single-column grid below about 700 px (grid-template-columns: 1fr).

title: Delete control is a div with no role, no name and no keyboard access, and is invisible until mouse hover
evidence: app.js:12 is a div with an onclick. styles.css:12 sets .del to opacity 0 and shows it only on li:hover. There is no tabindex or role, and the emoji is the only content. WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 (A), 1.4.1 and 2.5.1 on touch.
failing_case: On a phone there is no hover, so no delete control ever appears. A keyboard user can't reach it. A screen-reader user hears nothing meaningful.
remediation: Use a button with aria-label 'Delete note: <title>', visible at rest (or on :focus-within too), and a 44 px target.

title: Search responses are applied out of order and appended to a list that was already re-rendered
evidence: Every keystroke fires a fetch with no debounce and no AbortController. When the response arrives, the handler appends to #list whatever the list is now (app.js:46) without checking that q is still the current query. renderList only clears at the start of each input event. My mock responded instantly, so I did not reproduce the interleaving; this finding is traced.
failing_case: Type 'a' then 'ab'. Response 'ab' arrives, then the slower response 'a'. Both sets of shared rows are appended under the local results for 'ab'. Any renderList call (open note, delete) also wipes shared rows with no refetch.
remediation: Abort the previous request, debounce the input, and render shared results into their own container only if the response's query equals the current input value.

title: Viewport meta forbids pinch zoom
evidence: maximum-scale=1 on index.html:5 stops mobile browsers from zooming the page. WCAG 1.4.4 (AA).
failing_case: A low-vision user on a phone can't enlarge the 12 px hint or the note text.
remediation: Remove maximum-scale (and user-scalable=no if added later).

title: Title and body fields have no label, and search relies on its placeholder
evidence: index.html:13 (search: placeholder only), :19 (title: nothing) and :20 (body: nothing). There are no label elements and no aria-label anywhere in the page. WCAG 3.3.2 and 4.1.2.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' for the title and body fields. A speech-recognition user can't say a field's name to focus it.
remediation: Add visible or visually hidden label elements for search, title and body (for/id), and a placeholder for the title such as 'Untitled'.

title: No flush on pagehide or unload: edits in the last 500 ms are lost
evidence: The only write path for edits is the debounce timer. A grep of all four files shows no pagehide, beforeunload or visibilitychange listener.
failing_case: Type a sentence and refresh or close the tab within half a second. The timer never fires, and the sentence is gone.
remediation: Add pagehide and visibilitychange listeners that run the pending save synchronously.

title: Failed saves are swallowed while the UI says changes save automatically
evidence: persist() (store.js:23-27) catches every localStorage error, including QuotaExceededError and storage disabled in private mode, and ignores it. index.html:21 keeps showing 'Changes save automatically'. Traced; the quota test hook broke my own probe, so this was not driven to completion.
failing_case: localStorage is full. The user keeps typing, the hint says everything is saved, nothing is written, and the notes are gone on the next reload.
remediation: Return success or failure from persist(). Show 'Not saved: storage full or blocked' in a live region next to the hint, and keep the unsaved text in memory.

title: Focus indicator removed from every control with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:6 clears the outline on button, input and textarea. No :focus-visible style or box-shadow follows anywhere in styles.css (15 lines). WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing from Search to New note to Title to Body can't see which one has focus.
remediation: Delete the rule. Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px } for all controls.

title: Hint text and rank badges are far below 4.5:1 contrast
evidence: Computed against #fff: #ccc is about 1.6:1 (styles.css:15) and #bbb is about 1.9:1 (styles.css:11, the #rank badge). The borders on inputs (#eee) are also near-invisible, about 1.2:1. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA), and 1.4.11 for the input borders.
failing_case: The 'Changes save automatically' status, the only save feedback, is nearly unreadable for any user in daylight or with low vision.
remediation: Use at least #595959 on white for the hint and #767676 or darker for the badge. Use a border of at least 3:1 (#767676) on the inputs.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: renderList sorts the whole array once per row and uses innerHTML += in the loop
evidence: app.js:7-13: for each shown note it copies and sorts all notes, then re-parses the whole list through list.innerHTML +=. That is O(n² log n) work, and it runs on every search keystroke, note open and delete. Driven: renderList('') took 57 ms with 100 notes and 4,987 ms with 1,000 notes.
failing_case: A user with 500 to 1,000 notes types in the search box. Each keystroke freezes the page for seconds.
remediation: Sort once outside the loop and build a Map of id to rank. Build the rows into a DocumentFragment and assign once.

quote: const note = { id: Date.now(), title: 'Untitled', body: '', updated: Date.now() };
title: Date.now() ids collide, and deleteNote then deletes both notes
evidence: Driven: with Date.now fixed to the same value, two createNote() calls gave two notes with id 5. Calling deleteNote on the first left notes.length at 0, because the filter on n.id !== id removes both. openNote's find also always returns the first match.
failing_case: Double-click New (or a script, import or two tabs creates notes in the same millisecond). The two notes share an id, and deleting either one erases both permanently.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID(), or a counter checked against existing ids. Migrate duplicate ids on load.

title: Saving never re-renders the list, so the title and rank stay stale
evidence: The save timer updates the note but never calls renderList. Driven: set the title of note 'A' to 'Renamed' and waited 800 ms. The list still read 'A #1'.
failing_case: Rename a note. The sidebar shows the old name until some other action re-renders. Edited notes keep an out-of-date '#rank' badge.
remediation: Return a saved event from the store and have the view re-render, or call renderList from the same place that persists.

title: One click permanently deletes a note with no confirmation or undo
evidence: removeNote (app.js:23-28) calls deleteNote, which persists immediately (store.js:29-32). There is no confirm, no undo, and no 'Deleted' message. The delete target sits next to the title, on a row where any click otherwise opens the note.
failing_case: A mis-click on the trash icon deletes a long note. Nothing can bring it back.
remediation: Keep the deleted note for about 10 seconds behind an 'Undo' toast, or ask for confirmation naming the note.

title: Shared-search failures are only logged, and a non-OK status is never checked
evidence: app.js:44-47 never checks res.ok, and any failure is written to the console only. A 500 with an HTML body ends in a JSON parse error that is logged. A 200 with a JSON object that is not an array breaks shared.map and is also logged.
failing_case: The server returns 502 while the user searches. The list shows only local results with no hint that shared notes are unavailable. The user concludes that nothing shared matches.
remediation: Check res.ok and show 'Shared notes unavailable. Try again' in a status line, with the cause.

quote: button { background: #6366f1; color: #fff; border: 0; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 8px; }
title: White text on the indigo button and on the hero gradient is under 4.5:1
evidence: Computed: #fff on #6366f1 is 4.47:1, so the 14 px button label fails by a hair. The hero paragraph, white on #8b5cf6 (styles.css:3), is about 4.2:1 at normal size. WCAG 1.4.3.
failing_case: Low-vision user reads the New note button label and the hero paragraph with difficulty. They fail the AA threshold.
remediation: Darken the button to #4f46e5 or darker, and use a darker hero gradient end colour (#6d28d9) for white text.

quote: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Placeholder lorem ipsum text is shipped in the visible hero
evidence: index.html:11 renders Latin filler as the product tagline, under a 'Welcome to NoteMaster' heading. The hero uses about 120 px of vertical space on an app whose main task is the note list.
failing_case: Every visitor sees 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' as the first sentence.
remediation: Delete the hero, or replace the text with one real line. Give the page a heading that names the task.
